name: LML rules

rules.description: Each <section> requires exactly one <title>, and that title must be the first non-whitespace child.
Every <orderedlist> or <itemizedlist> must contain at least one <listitem>; each list item must have real content.

A <listitem> may contain only <para>, <mediaobject>, and nested <orderedlist>/<itemizedlist> elements as direct children -- no bare text and nothing else directly inside it. At least one of these is required; multiple are allowed (for example a <para> followed by a sublist). Treated as the complete allowed set for now -- covers the cases interns actually hit.
A <listitem> must not be empty (no content at all).
Every <imageobject> must be nested inside a <mediaobject>.
A <mediaobject> must include <imageobject> and <imagedata>, and <imagedata> must include fileref.
A table must contain <tbody>, each row must be a <tr> with <td> or <th> cells, and bare text inside a cell is not allowed.

rules.confidence: ~90%, confirmed once -- verify against a second captioned table
rules.description: A table's root element depends on whether it has a caption, matching real DocBook semantics: no <caption> -> <informaltable> (the norm); has a <caption> -> a formal <table>. Both use the identical tr/th/td content model -- this is not CALS, and a bare <table> should not be treated as a mistake. A generated <xml:id> on the table (e.g. so it can be targeted by an <xref> from another topic via Paligo's "Generate ID" action) is normal and not itself a sign of a bad paste.
Inline-only elements such as <emphasis role="bold"> and <guilabel> are allowed only where the rules permit them.
Current error conditions include missing titles, misplaced titles, missing list items, missing mediaobject/imageobject/imagedata, and raw text in cells.
Current warning conditions include unknown elements, empty paras, empty list items, inconsistent table column counts, multiple title elements in the same section, and unknown inline role values.

notes: This JSON file is the source of truth for the rule catalog -- rules are written directly here, not in a separate prose doc.

Severity scale (rules opt in via a "severity" field; absent means treat as an error for now): error (blocks save / structurally broken) > warning (real problem, not fatal) > caution (structurally valid, still worth flagging).

xref/indexterm/primary/secondary are recognized (tags.inline) but deliberately have no dedicated rules: what interns paste in always traces back to PDF-extracted content, which never produces indexing or cross-references. Kept in the vocabulary only so they don't false-flag as unknown elements in real topics that already use them.

Dropped rules, 2026-09-11 -- admonitions-para, table-border-pairing, section-not-empty, listitem-empty-para. Same reasoning as xref/indexterm above, plus scope: this tool's job is catching PDF-extracted content pasted into the wrong spot, not every theoretically-invalid document. The Extract tool never produces admonitions, and always emits the one correct frame/rules pair on every table it makes -- so neither failure mode can actually happen via a bad paste. section-not-empty/listitem-empty-para are real but merely cosmetic (still saveable, just thin) and not the paste-corruption class this tool exists for. note/warning/caution stay in tags.admonitions so an already-authored admonition elsewhere in the topic doesn't false-flag as unknown -- only the dedicated content-model rule for them is gone.
